report.source_text: The patient received oral prednisolone at an initial dosage of 35 mg/day (1 mg/kg/day). This helped in rapid epithelialisation of the erosions on the back. The intraoral erosions diminished significantly in 2 weeks, and the dose was tapered to 30 mg/day. A marked improvement in the lesions was observed on subsequent follow-up. The patient is currently on prednisolone treatment (15 mg/day), and to date, no other lesions have been reported.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Mucosal-dominant pemphigus vulgaris with minimal skin lesions
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 90-year-old Japanese woman presented with a 3-month history of painful gingivae progressing to 3 weeks of painful oral erosions following easily ruptured vesicles on buccal mucosa and tongue, causing difficulty eating. Physical examination revealed extensive oral erosions/desquamation with positive Nikolsky sign and minimal skin involvement (few erythematous back erosions). Gingival biopsy demonstrated suprabasal acantholysis with intraepithelial cleavage. Direct immunofluorescence confirmed intercellular IgG and C3 deposition. Serology showed elevated anti-Dsg3 (126 U/mL) with borderline anti-Dsg1 (21 U/mL), supporting the mucosal-dominant phenotype. The patient responded rapidly to oral prednisolone 35 mg/day with epithelialization of skin erosions and significant improvement of oral lesions within 2 weeks, successfully tapered to 15 mg/day maintenance without recurrence.
